claim: DODD 5400.07 reissued the DoD FOIA Program effective 5 April 2019.
quote: April 5, 2019

claim: The prior DoD 5400.7-R regulation was superseded by DODD 5400.07.
quote: DoD Manual 5400.07, “DoD Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Program,” January 25, 2017
fix: The directive reissues the 2005 DoDD 5400.07. It does not mention DoD 5400.7-R. Procedures sit in 32 CFR Part 286 and DoD Manual 5400.07 (2017). Cite those and fix the privacy page, which still routes FOIA review per DoD 5400.7-R.

claim: DODD 5400.07 and 5 USC 552(b) provide the nine FOIA exemptions and segregability rules.
quote: provides DoD records requested by members of the public, unless those records are exempt from disclosure in accordance with Section (b) of the FOIA.
fix: The directive states the exemption duty by reference only. The nine exemptions come from 5 USC 552(b). Segregability and fees sit in DoD Manual 5400.07 and 32 CFR 286. Fix the cites on lines 49, 67, 70, 72, 74, 97 and 106.

claim: The FOIA fee schedule and fee waiver criteria sit in DODD 5400.07.
quote: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 32, Part 286
fix: Cite 32 CFR 286 and DoD Manual 5400.07 for fees.

claim: On appeal the FOIA appeal authority reviews the IDA decision and renders a written decision per DODD 5400.07.
quote: serve as, or appoint another component official as, the component FOIA appellate authority.
fix: Add the component head appointment of the appellate authority.

claim: The DoD FOIA Annual Report goes to DOJ per DODD 5400.07 paragraph 4.
quote: Submits the DoD FOIA Annual Report and other reports as required by Section (e) of the FOIA to the Attorney General of the United States.
fix: The CMO submits the report under paragraph 2.1.c. The directive has no paragraph 4 on reporting. Units do not file it.

claim: The Initial Denial Authority is designated under SECNAVINST 5720.42F.
fix: SECNAVINST 5720.42F is not in the archive. DoDD 5400.07 says component heads administer the program and publish guidance (para 2.5.a). Verify the IDA designation in the DON instruction.

claim: The unit FOIA officer reviews records for exemption applicability.
quote: Administer the DoD FOIA Program within their component, to include publishing any additional guidance necessary for the implementation of this directive.
fix: Cite the DON instruction for the unit FOIA officer role.

claim: T&R event 0102-GENA-1003 Supervise Congressional or Special Interest Inquiries.
quote: 0102-GENA-1003:  Supervise Congressional/Special Interest Inquiries

claim: MCO 5740.4 is the Marine Corps Liaison to Congress order.
quote: RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SURVEYS AND INVESTIGATIONS STAFF, HOUSE APPROPRIATIONS COMMITTEE
fix: MCO 5740.4B covers the House Appropriations Committee Surveys and Investigations Staff. It is not a congressional liaison order. Fix the title or the citation.

claim: Exemption b(3) covers statutes such as 10 USC 130b.
quote: Exempts DoD critical infrastructure security information from release under the FOIA pursuant to Section 130e of Title 10, U.S.C.
fix: The directive itself cites 10 USC 130e and 10 USC 2254a as b(3) exemptions. Add them.

claim: SECNAVINST 5720.42F is the DON FOIA implementation.
fix: Not in the archive.

claim: SECNAVINST 5211.5F is the DON Privacy Program, while the privacy page cites SECNAVINST 5211.5 with no letter.
fix: Not in the archive. Use one edition letter on both pages.

claim: Route every FOIA request to legal for redaction per DOD 5400.7-R.
quote: DoD Manual 5400.07, “DoD Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Program,” January 25, 2017
fix: Cite DoDD 5400.07, DoD Manual 5400.07 and 32 CFR 286. The FOIA page on this site says 5400.7-R is superseded.

claim: Brief a suspected or confirmed PII breach to the unit security manager within 24 hours per SECNAVINST 5211.5.
quote: Ensure that security incidents (e.g., malicious code, attacks, intrusions, violations, spillages, PII breaches, etc.) are reported to the MCNOSC DCOS in a timely manner
fix: MCO 5239.2B says PII breaches go to the MCNOSC in a timely manner and sets no 24 hour figure. SECNAVINST 5211.5 is not in the archive. Cite the DON breach reporting message and its time limit.

claim: Encrypt PII in transit and at rest per MCO 5239.2B.
quote: Users shall digitally sign and encrypt all sensitive information on external media or in email exchanges
fix: Add FIPS 140-2 validated encryption with CAC or alternate token.

claim: Validate need-to-know per MCO 5239.2B Chapter 4.
quote: MARINE CORPS CYBERSECURITY
fix: MCO 5239.2B has no chapter 4 on need-to-know. Cite the paragraph or drop the chapter.

claim: Limit OMPF read access to records billet holders per MCO P1070.12K Chapter 3.
fix: MCO P1070.12K is not cached for this cluster. Verify chapter 3 against the order.

claim: NAVMC 3500.3E event 0102-GENA-1015 covers Privacy Act and HIPAA.
quote: 0102-GENA-1015:  Manage Marine Online (MOL) modules
fix: Event 0102-GENA-1015 is Manage Marine Online modules. Event 0102-GENA-2102 is Manage Disclosure of Personally Identifiable Information. Use 2102.

claim: Run annual Privacy Act training per SECNAVINST 5211.5.
fix: Not in the archive.

claim: NAVMC 118 (11) Page 11 documents Privacy Act training.
HIPAA controls apply to medical data held in MCTFS by clerks.
fix: Cite DoD 6025.18 and MCO 5239.2B. HIPAA applies to covered entities, not S-1 sections.

claim: MCO 5239.2B is the Marine Corps Cybersecurity Program.
quote: MARINE CORPS CYBERSECURITY

claim: A chaplain can receive a Restricted Report.
quote: However, a chaplain cannot accept a Restricted or Unrestricted Report.
fix: Remove chaplain and SVC from the list. Only the SARC, a SAPR VA and, for Restricted Reports, healthcare personnel take a report. Chaplains and VLCs help the victim reach the SARC. A disclosure to a chaplain files no report.

claim: The Special Victims’ Counsel can receive a Restricted Report.
quote: A VLC cannot accept a Restricted or Unrestricted Report.
fix: Remove SVC from the list of report recipients. The VLC facilitates contact with a SARC or SAPR VA.

claim: Restricted Reporting triggers no command notification.
quote: Only installation commands will be notified of Restricted Reports, without any PII, and only for the purpose of enhancing preventative measures
fix: The installation command learns a Restricted Report exists, without PII. Reword to say the victim identity and details stay confidential.

claim: Anyone in the chain of command can receive an Unrestricted Report.
quote: Disclosure of a sexual assault incident to others, with the exception of chaplains, Victim’s Legal Counsel (VLC), and healthcare personnel

claim: A Restricted Report converts to Unrestricted at any time and the reverse is generally not possible.
quote: When an Unrestricted Report is elected, the report cannot be converted to a Restricted Report.

claim: An SVC is available only after the victim files a report and is identified as a qualifying victim.
quote: Victims must be informed of the availability of legal assistance and the right to consult with a Special Victims’ Counsel (SVC)/Victims’ Legal Counsel (VLC)
fix: A victim consults an SVC or VLC before any report. The Marine Corps calls the role the Victims’ Legal Counsel. Say a victim reaches the VLC without filing a report.

claim: A victim may request expedited transfer after any report.
quote: processing of transfers requested by victims who have filed an Unrestricted Report of sexual assault.
fix: Expedited transfer covers victims who filed an Unrestricted Report. A Restricted Report does not qualify. Add the requirement.

claim: Article 6b gives the victim eight rights.
quote: The right to be informed in a timely manner of any plea agreement, separation-in-lieu-of-trial agreement, or non-prosecution agreement relating to the offense
fix: Article 6b now lists nine rights in the UCMJ text of the 2024 MCM. Add the right to timely notice of plea, separation-in-lieu-of-trial and non-prosecution agreements.

claim: The right to be heard covers hearings on detention, plea, sentencing, public release, or parole.
quote: The right to be reasonably heard at any of the following: (A) A public hearing concerning the continuation of confinement prior to trial of the
fix: The right to be heard covers pretrial confinement hearings, sentencing hearings and service clemency and parole board proceedings. Plea is not listed.

claim: A SAFE is best conducted within 96 hours.
fix: No archived paragraph sets a 96 hour window. The only 96 hour figure covers DSAID data entry in deployed locations. Remove the figure or cite the DoD SAFE protocol.

claim: A SAFE is available under both Restricted and Unrestricted reporting.
quote: the SARC, assigned SAPR VA, and/or healthcare personnel may not disclose confidential communications or Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) Kit information

claim: DoD Safe Helpline is 1-877-995-5247.
fix: Verify against the Safe Helpline site.

claim: Unrestricted reports lead to a possible MPO and the MPO is a UCMJ offense to violate.
quote: DD 2873, Military Protective Order (MPO)

claim: Sexual harassment and domestic violence are SVC qualifying offenses in some circumstances.
fix: Cite MCO 5800.16 Vol 4 eligibility rules.

claim: SVC communications are privileged under Military Rule of Evidence 502.
fix: Cite MRE 502 in the MCM.

claim: Marine Corps role is the Special Victims’ Counsel.
quote: Marine Corps Victims’ Legal Counsel Organization
fix: The Marine Corps office is the Victims’ Legal Counsel Organization and its counsel are VLCs. Use VLC with SVC in parentheses.

claim: Investigation typically takes weeks to months.
A disclosure to a person in the chain of command may already trigger Unrestricted Reporting.
quote: Disclosure of a sexual assault incident to others, with the exception of chaplains, Victim’s Legal Counsel (VLC), and healthcare personnel
